title: Access
audience: For everyone: who may do what, on the logic panel and the three built admin screens.

sections.heading: Principles
lines: This page answers the 7 Oct 2026 call: "what kind of roles, what kind of access, what kind of permissions".
A few people (7 Oct 2026 call): two working roles, the Principal officer and the Logic analyst, plus Compliance and Read only. At launch, two people run the panel; one of them can publish.
Ten fixed roles; no one can make a new one. A person holds one or more, and no one gets rights outside their roles.
Two people on every release, whatever roles they hold: the maker is never the checker, and only the Principal officer publishes. The one exception: an urgent hold (see Approval).
The server checks the role on every request and every change; the screen only mirrors it. A greyed-out button is never the real check.
Everything is logged, refused attempts too. Releases and plan snapshots are never edited; a correction is a new record.

sections.heading: The roles
lines: Principal officer: the only role that publishes a change. Also manages staff and roles.
Logic analyst: edits the rules in drafts; runs checks and impact preview.
Compliance: signs Assumptions and Risk profiling changes before they are published, and is told of every other release as it goes out.
A new working role starts only once Compliance signs it: proposed (LQ42).
Adviser takes calls, Call centre works the call tasks, Support answers tickets.
Ops: adds facts to unmapped ISINs (L04b) and queues each release's client email in {I14}.
Read only: product and tech sit here. Reads, never changes anything.
Marketing and Finance: no access to the logic panel; their admin screen rights are in the table by screen.
In the examples, staff are named by role and number (Principal officer 01, Logic analyst 01); no real person is drawn.

sections.heading: What each role may do, by screen
lines: Built from the screens files, so it is never typed twice. First every Logic tab screen in order, variants included: the role and writes fields of data/logic_screens.json. Then M03, M07 and M10, as they stand in data/admin_screens.json.
Cells: act (the role makes changes there; the Writes column says which), read, none, and "-" where the admin screen does not name the role.
"read, own people" ("own" for short): the role reads its own clients only. "read masked": a masked view, client names left out. The table by action calls them "read, own clients" and "masked view".
On L02, L03, L14, L04, L09, L07 and their variants, read for Adviser, Call centre, Ops and Support means the rules in use and their reasons only; draft rows never reach them.
On L08 the Logic analyst sees the releases and the versions plans are on, not the audit trail. On L13, the staff list and the roles table, not the access reviews.
The Writes column lists each write in the screens file's words: the action (its event; the roles that may do it).

lines: A draft goes: open, checked, impact preview done, waiting for approval, approved, published. Sent back, it is open again. A draft can also be discarded.
To be decided: which other changes Compliance must sign (LQ45).
Approval covers the changes, the rollout and the reason clients read. Changing any of them after approval sends it back.

The urgent path: an urgent hold by the Principal officer alone folds steps 1 to 8 into one action. Besides the hold, it may carry only the fund weights needed to pass the limits (L09). Compliance is told at once.
A second person, not the one who placed it, ratifies it within two working days. If not, it stays in force, shown as overdue on L08, L10 and L11 (LQ30). The Logic analyst may only ask for one (LQ25).
With two people at launch, every release needs both, except an urgent hold. To be decided: what happens when the Principal officer is away (LQ7).
The 7 Oct 2026 call asked for this step-by-step flow. Its nine steps were set while building, in the logic plan of 8 Oct 2026, and are open to veto.

lines: The audit trail: who, role, when, what, before, after, reason. Refused attempts too, marked as refused (L08).
The Principal officer and Compliance read and export the audit trail; Read only reads it; the Logic analyst does not see it.

The access review covers each person's roles, status (active, suspended or revoked), who added them and when, last sign-in, and whether two-step sign-in is on. At launch a list and the audit trail serve; the screen can follow.
In the examples, access review 1 on 15 Jul 2027 suspended Adviser 06, idle 90 days.
To be decided: the idle timeout, one session at a time, how old the 2FA may be (LQ41).

sections.heading: The client app
lines: The app has one kind of user, the client. What a client can do depends on their tier: what they are entitled to, not a role. Each board screen already shows it (LQ40).
The logic panel never answers a request carrying a client's token. It is a separate staff web app, desktop only (as on the board's L01), kept apart by its own web address and the type of token.
